DIRECTING THE RESPONDENTS TO GRANT COMPENSATION IN RESPECT ACQUISITION OF 19 GUNTAS OF LAND IN SY NO.33 OF SONAPPANAHALLI, JALA HOBLI, BANGALORE NORTH TALUK.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING IN B-GROUP, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER This writ petition is filed for following relies:
i) Issue a writ, Direction or order in the nature of mandamus by directing the respondents to implement Annexure-M letter bearing No.LAQ/NH-7/Hy- Dr/Misc/155/2020-21 dt:11.03.2022;
ii) Issue any other Writ, Direction or Order directing the respondents to grant compensation in respect of acquisition of 19 guntas of land in Sy.no.33 of Sonnappanahalli, Jala Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk; etc. NC: 2023:KHC:45616 2.

Smt.Sona Vakkund, learned counsel for petitioner submitted that petitioner was owner of land Smt Basamma vs National Highway Authority Of India on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87673243/
2 measuring 2 acres in Sy.no.33/1 of Sonnappanahalli village, Jala Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk,
having purchased it under registered sale deed dated 31.03.1983.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was submitted that at time of phodi of her land, it was noticed by her that some portion of land was used by respondent no.1 for formation of service road of N.H.7 (Hyderabad - Bengaluru).
Accordingly, she filed representation to respondent no.2 for compensation as per Annexure-C dated 13.12.2017.

Subsequently, after survey,
JMC report at Annexure - K was prepared by Taluk Surveyor, Yelahanka, indicating that land to an extent of 19 guntas out of petitioner's land was under possession of respondent no.1.
3.
Thereafter petitioner submitted representation to respondent no.1 on 19.02.2021.
In pursuance of same, respondent no.1 addressed correspondences to respondent no.2 about reasons for delay in issuing notification under Section 3A of National Highways Act.

In response, respondent no.2 informed respondent no.1 about having got land measured by deputing surveyor and finding that some extent of land was utilised for service road and seeking for condonation NC: 2023:KHC:45616 of delay in sending proposal under Section 3A of National Highways Act.
Alleging that no further steps were taken, petitioner has approached this Court seeking for appropriate direction.

4. On other hand Sri Shobith Shetty, learned counsel for respondents no.1 and 2 submitted that before counsel for petitioner seek for issuance of direction, respondent was required to verify whether land stated to be utilised by respondent no.1 was subject matter of earlier acquisition or whether any land belonging to petitioner was utilised without acquisition and in case, if it was found that respondent had utilised same without acquisition, appropriate steps would be taken by respondent within reasonable time.

5. Heard learned counsel and writ petition record.
6.

From above, petitioner's grievance is that even after having found that portion of petitioner's land was utilised by respondent no.1 for forming service road i.e.N.H.-7 respondent had not taken steps for acquisition and for payment of compensation.
While it is case of respondents that same has to be notified after factual verification as stated above.

In view of above writ petition is disposed of directing respondents to take further steps in pursuance of correspondent at Annexure-M within a period of four months from date of receipt of certified copy of this order after ascertaining whether any portion of petitioner's land has been utilised by respondent no.1 for formation of service road without acquisition, if necessary by fresh survey, in presence of petitioner and finding utilisation without acquisition.

In other case, respondents would be at liberty to issue well reasoned endorsement to petitioner with particulars if petitioner's land is acquired and utilized, by due process of law by providing details of compensation paid/deposited.
Needless to state that while issuing said endorsement, respondents shall be required to traverse earlier survey reports to contrary.
